page: Amazon Web Services m5a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor featuring two physical x86_64 cores configured with simultaneous multithreading to deliver four dedicated virtual CPUs. The memory subsystem provides 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache capacity includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache. Hardware acceleration includes AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instructions, though AVX-512 extensions are absent.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring attached Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data. Network performance is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Graphics acceleration is not present, with zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reflect legacy-generation compute characteristics. Synthetic compute evaluation shows lower-tier throughput, with Geekbench single-core scoring 725.0 and multi-core reaching 1744.0, while PassMark CPU registers 3670.17. PassMark CPU encryption achieves average relative output at 3248.98, supported by hardware AES and SHA-NI flags. Memory bandwidth registers 30.01 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 14.45 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests show 2.51 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.98 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Relative to newer hardware generations, m5a.xlarge offers an economical compute footprint for steady-state workloads that do not demand cutting-edge single-thread execution speeds or high-throughput vector extensions. The instance profile is aligned with non-critical development and test environments, small-scale web servers, lightweight background worker processes, and microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring four vCPUs and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with two physical cores supporting dedicated threads via the AWS Nitro System. The instance contains no bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-level execution throughput, with Geekbench single-core at 725.0 and multi-core at 1744.0, while hardware cryptographic instructions support moderate encryption results. With lower instruction throughput compared to modern architectures, this server offers a cost-effective resource tier for standard operational tasks such as small web services, development environments, and lightweight containerized workloads.
